plan_a_advantages: Includes longer runs with moderate intensity, building a stronger aerobic base.
Features a controlled tempo run, introducing a key element for speed development.
plan_b_advantages: Emphasizes low fatigue, potentially beneficial for injury prevention.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates longer runs with moderate intensity, which is crucial for building the aerobic base and trail-specific endurance needed for faster times. Plan B focuses almost entirely on easy runs and a single tempo session, lacking the volume and varied intensity required to truly improve speed. While Plan B prioritizes low fatigue, Plan A’s structured approach with longer runs and a controlled tempo session will more effectively challenge the athlete and promote physiological adaptations for faster trail running.
